name: Granby Roll to Guard
summary: A Granby roll recovers guard through a shoulder-and-upper-back roll when the head and limbs are free; a Buggy Choke holder must release the arm-and-leg loop before considering that movement.
description: A Granby needs a free head and limbs for a shoulder-supported roll. Release the Buggy arm-and-leg loop before considering a separately established roll.
overview:
The bottom player must have space to move over the shoulder without a trapped neck, arm or knee. Buggy Choke bottom is the holder of the choke, not a turtle defender under an upper-body ride. The reviewed Buggy instruction supports framing and recovering guard when the opponent disengages; it does not establish a direct Granby entry.

Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam. Create distance while keeping the head free and the knees available to return inside. Use a shoulder roll only if a coach has established safe space and an untrapped upper back.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Kade and Tye Ruotolo — OG Buggy Choke](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zixbOyLpoOc); [Jay Rodriguez — three Buggy Choke mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjKERx4N4mY).

While the Buggy loop is still in place, forearm and shin hip control can limit the top player rising; release immediately if you are lifted. For guard retention, open that loop and place forearms between the bodies to manage chest pressure. Move the hips to recover knee space first; a shoulder roll remains conditional on a free head and limbs.

defender.overview:

Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg. Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes. Treat the choke as live even though you hold top side control.

Free the head-and-arm enclosure before changing to north-south or chasing another pin. Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape. Stop before dizziness or loss of normal responsiveness; top position does not make a secured choke safe.
